titleStmt.title: Notes of Telephone Conversation Between the Executive Secretary of the Department of State (Read) and Chester Cooper of the National Security Council Staff

div.head: 53. Notes of Telephone Conversation Between the Executive Secretary of the Department of State (Read) and Chester Cooper of the National Security Council Staff
div.p: Chet Cooper called to double talk following message:

The UK and Cooper think that Kosygin may have indicated “a bite.” He indicated to Wilson in talks this afternoon (London time) considerable interest in our Phase A-Phase B proposal and committed himself to send it in cable form to Hanoi with his endorsement. Kosygin is leaving London at 10:30 p.m. London time tonight and wants an agreed text ASAP.
Suggested text (which will be flashed to us) consists of five short lettered paragraphs.

list.label: a.
list.item: The US will stop the bombing as soon as it has been assured that infiltration by the North will stop and this assurance can be given privately.
list.label: b.
list.item: Within a few days to be agreed upon by the parties, the US will stop augmenting its forces in the South and North Viet Nam will stop infiltration.
list.label: c.
list.item: What the US does will of course be immediately apparent but no public rationale will be stated at the time.
list.label: d.
list.item: What North Viet Nam does will be more difficult to observe but the US will not demand a public statement that they have taken the required action.
list.label: e.
list.item: These assurances can be given and exchanged by the USG and the DRV directly or through the Soviets and/or British.

note.p: Source: Johnson Library, National Security File, Country File, Vietnam, Sunflower & Sunflower Plus. Top Secret; Sunflower Plus. The document is undated but references in the text confirm the date as February 10. Cooper was in London; Read was in Washington.

A Flash telegram, telegram 6456 from London, February 10, 1900Z, contained these five elements slightly rephrased. (National Archives and Records Administration, RG 59, Central Files 1967–69, POL 27–14 VIET/SUNFLOWER)
